q: If one-third of one-fourth of a number is 15, then three-tenth of that number is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{be}}\,x \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{1}{3}\,{\text{of}}\,\frac{1}{{4\,}}\,{\text{of}}\,x = 15\\ & \Rightarrow \, x = 15 \times 12 = 180 \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{required}}\,{\text{number}} \\ & = {\frac{3}{{10}} \times 180} \\ & = 54 \end{aligned}$$

q: Three times the first of three consecutive odd integers is 3 more than twice the third. The third integer is:
s: Let the three integers be x , x + 2 and x + 4 Then, 3 x = 2( x + 4) + 3 ⇔ x = 11 ∴ Third integer = x + 4 = 15

q: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the positions of its digits is 36. What is the difference between the two digits of that number?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y . Then, (10 x + y ) - (10 y + x ) = 36 ⇒ 9( x - y ) = 36 ⇒ x - y = 4

q: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the digits is 36. What is the difference between the sum and the difference of the digits of the number if the ratio between the digits of the number is 1 : 2 ?
s: Since the number is greater than the number obtained on reversing the digits, so the ten's digit is greater than the unit's digit. Let ten's and unit's digits be 2 x and x respectively. Then, (10 × 2 x + x ) - (10 x + 2 x ) = 36 ⇒ 9 x = 36 ⇒ x = 4 ∴ Required difference = (2 x + x ) - (2 x - x ) = 2 x = 8

q: A two-digit number is such that the product of the digits is 8. When 18 is added to the number, then the digits are reversed. The number is:
s: Let the ten's and unit digit be x and $$\frac{8}{x}$$ respectively $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then,}} \\ & \left( {10x + \frac{8}{x}} \right) + 18 = 10 \times \frac{8}{x} + x \\ & \Rightarrow 10{x^2} + 8 + 18x = 80 + {x^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 9{x^2} + 18x - 72 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} + 2x - 8 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x + 4} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 2 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ first digit will be 2 and second digit will be 4. i.e digit is 24.

q: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 15 and the difference between the digits is 3. What is the two-digit number?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, x + y = 15 and x - y = 3 or y - x = 3 Solving x + y = 15 and x - y = 3, we get: x = 9, y = 6 Solving x + y = 15 and y - x = 3, we get: x = 6, y = 9 So, the number is either 96 or 69 Hence, the number cannot be determined.

q: The sum of the squares of three numbers is 138, while the sum of their products taken two at a time is 131. Their sum is:
s: Let the numbers be a , b and c Then, a 2 + b 2 + c 2 = 138 and ( ab + bc + ca ) = 131 (a + b + c) 2 = a 2 + b 2 + c 2 + 2( ab + bc + ca ) = 138 + 2 x 131 = 400 ⇒ ( a + b + c ) = $$\sqrt {400}$$ = 20

q: A number consists of two digits. If the digits interchange places and the new number is added to the original number, then the resulting number will be divisible by:
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y . Then, number = 10 x + y Number obtained by interchanging the digits = 10 y + x ∴ (10 x + y ) + (10 y + x ) = 11( x + y ), which is divisible by 11

q: In a two-digit, if it is known that its unit's digit exceeds its ten's digit by 2 and that the product of the given number and the sum of its digits is equal to 144, then the number is:
s: Let the ten's digit be x Then, unit's digit = x + 2 Number = 10 x + ( x + 2) = 11 x + 2 Sum of digits = x + ( x + 2) = 2 x + 2 ∴ (11 x + 2)(2 x + 2) = 144 ⇒ 22 x 2 + 26 x - 140 = 0 ⇒ 11 x 2 + 13 x - 70 = 0 ⇒ 11 x 2 + (35 - 22)x - 70 = 0 ⇒ 11 x 2 + 35x - 22x - 70 = 0 ⇒ ( x - 2)(11 x + 35) = 0 ⇒ x = 2 Hence, required number = 11 x + 2 = 24

q: Find a positive number which when increased by 17 is equal to 60 times the reciprocal of the number.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{be}}\,x \\ & {\text{Then}},\,x + 17 = \frac{{60}}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} + 17x - 60 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow (x + 20)(x - 3) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 3 \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two numbers is 9375 and the quotient, when the larger one is divided by the smaller, is 15. The sum of the numbers is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{and}}\,y \\ & {\text{Then}},\,xy = 9375\,{\text{and}}\,\frac{x}{y} = 15 \\ & \frac{{xy}}{{\left( {x/y} \right)}} = \frac{{9375}}{{15}} \\ & \Rightarrow {y^2} = 625 \\ & \Rightarrow y = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15y = \left( {15 \times 25} \right) = 375 \\ & \therefore {\text{Sum}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{number}} \\ & = x + y = 375 + 25 = 400 \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two numbers is 120 and the sum of their squares is 289. The sum of the number is:
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, x y = 120 and x 2 + y 2 = 289 ∴ ( x + y ) 2 = x 2 + y 2 + 2 x y = 289 + (2 x 120) = 529 ∴ x + y = $$\sqrt {529}$$ = 23

q: A number consists of 3 digits whose sum is 10. The middle digit is equal to the sum of the other two and the number will be increased by 99 if its digits are reversed. The number is:
s: Let the middle digit be x Then, 2 x = 10 or x = 5. So, the number is either 253 or 352 Since the number increases on reversing the digits, so the hundred's digits is smaller than the unit's digit. Hence, required number = 253

q: The sum of two number is 25 and their difference is 13. Find their product.
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, x + y = 25 and x - y = 13 4 x y = ( x + y ) 2 - ( x - y ) 2 = (25) 2 - (13) 2 = (625 - 169) = 456 ∴ x y = 114

q: What is the sum of two consecutive even numbers, the difference of whose squares is 84?
s: Let the numbers be x and x + 2. Then, ( x + 2) 2 - x 2 = 84 ⇒ 4 x + 4 = 84 ⇒ 4 x = 80 ⇒ x = 20. ∴ The required sum = x + ( x + 2) = 2 x + 2 = 42

q: The sum of twice a number and three times of 42 is 238. What is the sum of thrice the number and two times of 42 ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 2x + 3 \times 42 = 238 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2x + 126 = 238 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2x = 112 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 56 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required sum : $$\begin{aligned} & = 3x + 2 \times 42 \\ & = 3 \times 56 + 2 \times 42 \\ & = 168 + 84 \\ & = 252 \end{aligned}$$

q: By how much is $$\frac{3}{4}$$th of 568 lesser than $$\frac{7}{8}$$th of 1008 ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{7}{8}{\text{ of }}1008 - \frac{3}{4}{\text{ of }}568 \\ & = \left( {1008 \times \frac{7}{8}} \right) - \left( {568 \times \frac{3}{4}} \right) \\ & = 882 - 426 \\ & = 456 \end{aligned}$$

q: Thrice the square of a natural number decreased by 4 times the number is equal to 50 more than the number. The number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 3{x^2} - 4x = x + 50 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3{x^2} - 5x - 50 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {3x + 10} \right)\left( {x - 5} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 5 \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the greater of the two numbers whose product is 1092 and the sum of the two numbers exceeds their difference by 42 ?
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, $$xy = 1092.....(i)$$ And, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + y} \right) - \left( {x - y} \right) = 42 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2y = 42 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 21 \end{aligned}$$ Putting y = 21 in (i), we get : $$x = \frac{{1092}}{{21}} = 52$$ Hence, greater number = 52

q: The product of three consecutive even numbers when divided by 8 is 720. The product of their square roots is :
s: Let the numbers be x, x + 2 and x + 4 Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x\left( {x + 2} \right)\left( {x + 4} \right)}}{8} = 720 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x\left( {x + 2} \right)\left( {x + 4} \right) = 5760 \\ & \therefore \sqrt x \times \sqrt {\left( {x + 2} \right)} \times \sqrt {\left( {x + 4} \right)} \\ & = \sqrt {x\left( {x + 2} \right)\left( {x + 4} \right)} \\ & = \sqrt {5760} \\ & = 24\sqrt {10} \end{aligned}$$

q: The digit in the unit's place of a numbers is equal to the digit in the ten's place of half of that number and the digit in the ten's place of that number is less than the digit in unit's place of half of the number by 1. If the sum of the digits of the number is 7, then what is the number ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{10x + y}}{2} = 10y + \left( {x + 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 10x + y = 20y + 2x + 2 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 8x - 19y = 2.....(i) \\ & {\text{And}} \Leftrightarrow x + y = 7.....(ii) \end{aligned}$$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get : x = 5, y = 2 Hence, required number = 52

q: Of the three number, the sum of the first two is 73, the sum of the second and the third is 77 and the sum of the third and thrice the first is 104. The third number is ?
s: Let the numbers be x, y and z Then, $$\begin{aligned} & {\bf{x + y = 73}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 73 - x \\ & {\bf{y + z = 77 }} \\ & \Leftrightarrow z = 77 - y \\ & \Leftrightarrow z = 77 - \left( {73 - x} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow z = 4 + x \\ & {\bf{3x + z = 104}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3x + 4 + x = 104 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4x = 100 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 25 \\ & \because y = \left( {73 - 25} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 48 \\ & \because z = \left( {4 + 25} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow z = 29 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Third number = 29

q: The difference between a number and its three-fifths is 50, What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x - \frac{3}{5}x = 50 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{2}{5}x = 50 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{50 \times 5}}{2}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 125 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two-third of a positive number and $$\frac{25}{216}$$ of its reciprocal are equal, The number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{25}{216} \times \frac{1}{x} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} = \frac{{25}}{{216}} \times \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} = \frac{{25}}{{144}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \sqrt {\frac{{25}}{{144}}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{5}{{12}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between two integers is 5. Their product is 500. Find the numbers.
s: Let the integers be x and (x + 5) Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x\left( {x + 5} \right) = 500 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 5x - 500 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 25} \right)\left( {x - 20} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 20 \end{aligned}$$ So, the numbers are 20 and 25

q: What is the sum of two consecutive even numbers, the difference of whose squares is 84 ?
s: Let the numbers be x and x + 2 Then, (x + 2) 2 - x 2 = 84 ⇔ 4x + 4 = 84 ⇔ 4x = 80 ⇔ x = 20 ∴ Required sum = x + (x + 2) = 2x + 2 = 42

q: A certain number of two digits is three times the sum of its digits and if 45 be added to it, the digits are reversed. The number is ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 10x + y = 3\left( {x + y} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 7x - 2y = 0.....(i) \\ & 10x + y + 45 = 10y + x \\ & \Rightarrow y - x = 5.....(ii) \end{aligned}$$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get : x = 2 and y = 7 ∴ Required number = 27

q: If the product of two numbers is 5 and one of the number is $$\frac{3}{2}$$, then sum of two numbers is :
s: Let two numbers be a and b Given ab = 5 and a = $$\frac{3}{2}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow b = \frac{5}{a} \\ & \Rightarrow b = \frac{5}{{\frac{3}{2}}} \\ & \Rightarrow b = \frac{{5 \times 2}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow b = \frac{{10}}{3} \end{aligned}$$ Required sum of : ⇒ a + b = $$\frac{{3}}{2}$$ + $$\frac{{10}}{3}$$ L.C.M. of 2 and 3 = 6 ⇒ a + b = $$\frac{{9 + 20}}{6}$$ ⇒ a + b = $$\frac{{29}}{6}$$ ⇒ a + b = $$4\frac{{5}}{6}$$

q: If a number is added to two-fifths of itself, the value so obtained is 455. What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x + \frac{2}{5}x = 455 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{7}{5}x = 455 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{455 \times 5}}{7}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 325 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the whole number which when increased by 20 is equal to 69 times the reciprocal of the number.
s: Let the required number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x + 20 = \frac{{69}}{x} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 20x - 69 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 23x - 3x - 69 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x\left( {x + 23} \right) - 3\left( {x + 23} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 23} \right)\left( {x - 3} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\because x \ne - 23} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: If a number is multiplied by two-third of itself the value so obtained is 864. What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x \times \frac{2}{3}x = 864 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{2}{3}{x^2} = 864 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} = \left( {\frac{{864 \times 3}}{2}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} = 1296 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \sqrt {1296} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 36 \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two numbers is 9375 and the quotient, when the larger one is divided by the smaller, is 15. The sum of the numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, $$xy = 9375{\text{ and }}\frac{x}{y} = 15$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{xy}}{{\left( {\frac{x}{y}} \right)}} = \frac{{9375}}{{15}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {y^2} = 625 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 25 \\ & \therefore x = 15y \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15 \times 25 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 375 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Sum of the numbers : = 375 + 25 = 400

q: If the product of three consecutive integers is 120, then the sum of the integers is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 120: \\ & = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 5 \\ & = \left( {2 \times 2} \right) \times 5 \times \left( {2 \times 3} \right) \\ & = 4 \times 5 \times 6 \end{aligned}$$ Clearly, the three consecutive integers whose product is 120 are 4, 5 and 6 Required sum : = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15

q: A two-digit number is such that the product of the digits is 8. When 18 is added to the number, then the digits are reversed. The number is :
s: Let the ten's and unit's digits be $$x$$ and $$\frac{8}{x}$$ respectively Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {10x + \frac{8}{x}} \right) + 18 = 10 \times \frac{8}{x} + x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 10{x^2} + 8 + 18x = 80 + {x^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9{x^2} + 18x - 72 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 2x - 8 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 4} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2 \end{aligned}$$ So, ten's digit = 2 and unit's digit = 4 Hence, required number = 24

q: The sum of the squares of three numbers is 138, while the sum of their product taken two at a time is 131. Their sum is :
s: Let the numbers be a, b and c. Then, a 2 + b 2 + c 2 = 138 And (ab + bc + ca) = 131 ∴ (a + b + c) 2 = a 2 + b 2 + c 2 + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 138 + 2 × 131 = 400 ⇒ (a + b + c) = $$\sqrt {400}$$ = 20

q: The sum of the squares of two positive integers is 100 and the difference of their squares is 28. The sum of the numbers is ?
s: Let the positive integers be a and b where a > b According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & {a^2} + {b^2} = 100.....(\text{i}) \\ & {a^2} - {b^2} = 28.....(\text{ii}) \end{aligned}$$ By adding (i) and (ii), we get : $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {a^2} + {b^2} + {a^2} - {b^2} = 100 + 28 \\ & \Rightarrow 2{a^2} = 128 \\ & \Rightarrow {a^2} = \frac{{128}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow a = \sqrt {64} \\ & \Rightarrow a = 8 \end{aligned}$$ From equation (i) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {8^2} + {b^2} = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow {b^2} = 100 - 64 \\ & \Rightarrow b = \sqrt {36} \\ & \Rightarrow b = 6 \\ & \therefore a + b = 8 + 6 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 14 \end{aligned}$$

q: A number when multiplied by 13 is increased by 180. The number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 13x = x + 180 \\ & \Rightarrow 12x = 180 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{180}}{{12}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15 \end{aligned}$$

q: A positive number when decreased by 4 is equal to 21 times the reciprocal of the number. The number is ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x - 4 = \frac{{21}}{x} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - 4x - 21 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 7} \right)\left( {x + 3} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between two numbers is 1365. When the large number is divided by the smaller one, the quotient is 6 and the remainder is 15. The smaller number is :
s: Let the numbers be x and (x + 1365) Then, ⇒ x + 1365 = 6x + 15 ⇒ 5x = 1350 ⇒ x = 270

q: A number of two digits has 3 for its unit's digit, and the sum of digits is $$\frac{1}{7}$$ of the itself. The number is :
s: Let the ten's digit be x Then, number = 10x + 3 and Sum of digits = (x + 3) So, (x + 3) = $$\frac{1}{7}$$(10x + 3) ⇔ 7x + 21 = 10x + 3 ⇔ 3x = 18 ⇔ x = 6 Hence, the number is : = (10x + 3) = (10 × 6 + 3) = 63

q: In a three-digit number, the digit in the unit's place is 75% of the digit in the ten's place. The digit in the ten's place is greater than the digit in the hundred's place by 1. If the sum of the digits in the ten's place and the hundred's place is 15. What is the number ?
s: Let the hundred's digit = x Then, ten's digit = (x + 1) Unit's digit : $$\begin{aligned} & = 75\% {\text{ of }}\left( {x + 1} \right) \\ & = \frac{3}{4}\left( {x + 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {x + 1} \right) + x = 15 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2x = 14 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 7 \end{aligned}$$ So, hundred's digit = 7 Ten's digit = 8 Unit's digit : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{3}{4}\left( {x + 1} \right) \\ & = \frac{3}{4}\left( {7 + 1} \right) \\ & = \frac{3}{4}\left( 8 \right) \\ & = 6 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, required number = 786

q: The sum of two numbers is 37 and the difference of their squares is 185, then the difference between the two numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be a and b, where a > b According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & a + b = 37\& {a^2} - {b^2} = 185 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {a + b} \right)\left( {a - b} \right) = 185 \\ & \Rightarrow 37\left( {a - b} \right) = 185 \\ & \Rightarrow a - b = \frac{{185}}{{37}} \\ & \Rightarrow a - b = 5 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between $$\frac{3}{5}$$th of $$\frac{2}{3}$$rd of a number and $$\frac{2}{5}$$th of $$\frac{1}{4}$$th of the same number is 288. What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{3}{5}{\text{of }}\frac{2}{3}{\text{of }}x - \frac{2}{5}{\text{of }}\frac{1}{4}{\text{of }}x = 288 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x \times \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{3}} \right) - \left( {x \times \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{4}} \right) = 288 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{{10}}x = 288 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{3x}}{{10}} = 288 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{288 \times 10}}{3}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 960 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum and product of two numbers are 12 and 35 respectively. The sum of their reciprocals will be :
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & x + y = 12\,\, \& \,\, xy = 35 \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{{x + y}}{{xy}} = \frac{{12}}{{35}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between two numbers is 16. If one-third of the smaller number is greater than one-seventh of the larger number by 4, then the two numbers are :
s: Let the numbers be x and (x + 16) Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{3} - \frac{{\left( {x + 16} \right)}}{7} = 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 7x - 3\left( {x + 16} \right) = 84 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4x = 84 + 48 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4x = 132 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 33 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the numbers are 33 and 49

q: If a number of two digits is k times the sum of its digits, then the number formed by interchanging the digits is the sum of the digits multiplied by :
s: Let the ten's digit be x and the unit's digit be y Then, number = 10x + y $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 10x + y = k\left( {x + y} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow k = \frac{{10x + y}}{{x + y}} \end{aligned}$$ Number formed by interchanging the digits = 10y + x Let, 10y + x = h(x + y) Then, $$\begin{aligned} & h = \frac{{10y + x}}{{x + y}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{11\left( {x + y} \right) - \left( {10x + y} \right)}}{{x + y}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\, = 11 - \frac{{10x + y}}{{x + y}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\, = 11 - k \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two fractions is $$\frac{14}{15}$$ and their quotient is $$\frac{35}{24}$$. The greater fraction is :
s: Let the two fractions be a and b Then, $$\begin{aligned} & ab = \frac{{14}}{{15}}\, \& \, \frac{a}{b} = \frac{{35}}{{24}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{ab}}{{\left( {\frac{a}{b}} \right)}} = \left( {\frac{{14}}{{15}} \times \frac{{24}}{{35}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {b^2} = \frac{{16}}{{25}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow b = \frac{4}{5} \\ & {\text{So, }} \\ & \Leftrightarrow ab = \frac{{14}}{{15}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow a = \left( {\frac{{14}}{{15}} \times \frac{5}{4}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow a = \frac{7}{6} \end{aligned}$$ Since a > b, So, greater fraction is $$\frac{7}{6}$$

q: A man bought some eggs of which 10% are rotten. He gives 80% of the remainder to his neighbours. Now he is left out with 36 eggs. How many eggs he bought ?
s: Let the total number of eggs bought be a 10% of eggs are rotten ∴ Remaining eggs : $$\begin{aligned} & = a - 10\% {\text{ of }}a \\ & = a - \frac{{10a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{100a - 10a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{90a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{9a}}{{10}} \end{aligned}$$ Man gives 80% of $$\frac{{9a}}{{100}}$$ eggs to his neighbour $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{80}}{{100}} \times \frac{{9a}}{{10}} \\ & = \frac{{72a}}{{100}} \end{aligned}$$ Remaining eggs : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{9a}}{{10}} - \frac{{72a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{90a - 72a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{18a}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{9a}}{{50}} \end{aligned}$$ According the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{9a}}{{50}} = 36 \\ & \Rightarrow 9a = 36 \times 50 \\ & \Rightarrow a = \frac{{36 \times 50}}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow a = 200 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the total number of eggs bought be = 200

q: A number is double and 9 is added. If the resultant is trebled, it becomes 75. What is that number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, ⇔ 3(2x + 9) = 75 ⇔ 2x + 9 = 25 ⇔ 2x = 16 ⇔ x = 8

q: The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is thrice the difference of the number and its reciprocal. The number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x + \frac{1}{x} = 3\left( {x - \frac{1}{x}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{{x^2} + 1}}{x} = 3\left( {\frac{{{x^2} - 1}}{x}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 1 = 3{x^2} - 3 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2{x^2} = 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} = 2 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \sqrt 2 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of two numbers is 40 and their product is 375. What will be the sum of their reciprocals ?
A two-digit number is 7 times the sum of its two digits. The number that is formed by reversing its digits is 18 less than the original number. What is the number ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and the unit's digit be y Then, number = 10x + y $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 10x + y = 7\left( {x + y} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3x = 6y \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2y \end{aligned}$$ Number formed by reversing the digits = 10y + x $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {10x + y} \right) - \left( {10y + x} \right) = 18 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9x - 9y = 18 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x - y = 2 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2y - y = 2 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 2 \\ & {\text{So, }}x = 2y = 4 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, ∴ Required number = 10x + y = 40 + 2 = 42

q: If the difference between the reciprocal of a positive proper fraction and the fraction itself be $$\frac{9}{20}$$, then the fraction is :
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{a}{1}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{1}{a} - a = \frac{9}{{20}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{1 - {a^2}}}{a} = \frac{9}{{20}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 20 - 20{a^2} = 9a \\ & \Leftrightarrow 20{a^2} + 9a - 20 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 20{a^2} + 25a - 16a - 20 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5a\left( {4a + 5} \right) - 4\left( {4a + 5} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {4a + 5} \right)\left( {5a - 4} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow a = \frac{4}{5}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\because a \ne - \frac{5}{4}} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of two numbers is 75 and their difference is 25. The product of the two numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be a and b According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & a + b = 75 \\ & a - b = 25 \\ & \because {\left( {a + b} \right)^2} - {\left( {a - b} \right)^2} = 4ab \\ & \Rightarrow {75^2} - {25^2} = 4ab \\ & \Rightarrow 4ab = \left( {75 + 25} \right)\left( {75 - 25} \right) \\ & \left[ {\because {a^2} - {b^2} = \left( {a + b} \right)\left( {a - b} \right)} \right] \\ & \Rightarrow 4ab = 100 \times 50 \\ & \Rightarrow ab = \frac{{100 \times 50}}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow ab = 1250 \end{aligned}$$

q: Three-forth of a number is 60 more than its one-third. The number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{3}x = 60 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{5x}}{{12}} = 60 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{60 \times 12}}{5}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 144 \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two natural numbers is 17. Then, the sum of the reciprocals of their squares is :
s: Let the numbers be a and b Then, ab = 17 ⇒ a = 1 and b = 17 So, $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{{a^2}}} + \frac{1}{{{b^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{{a^2} + {b^2}}}{{{a^2}{b^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{{1^2} + {{\left( {17} \right)}^2}}}{{{{\left( {1 \times 17} \right)}^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{290}}{{289}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A number whose fifth part increase by 4 is equal to its fourth part diminished by 10, is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{5} + 4 = \frac{x}{4} - 10 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{4} - \frac{x}{5} = 14 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{{20}} = 14 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 14 \times 20 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 280 \end{aligned}$$

q: If $$2\frac{1}{2}$$ is added tp a number and the sum multiplied by $$4\frac{1}{2}$$ and 3 is added to the product and the sum is divided by $$1\frac{1}{5}$$, the quotient becomes 25. What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{4\frac{1}{2}\left( {x + 2\frac{1}{2}} \right) + 3}}{{1\frac{1}{5}}} = 25 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{\frac{9}{2}\left( {x + \frac{5}{2}} \right) + 3}}{{\frac{6}{5}}} = 25 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{9x}}{2} + \frac{{45}}{4} + 3 = 25 \times \frac{6}{5} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{9x}}{2} + \frac{{45}}{4} + 3 = 30 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{9x}}{2} = 30 - \frac{{57}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{9x}}{2} = \frac{{63}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{63}}{4} \times \frac{2}{9}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{7}{2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The product of two numbers is 120 and the sum of their square is 289. The sum of the numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, xy = 120 and x 2 + y 2 = 289 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\left( {x + y} \right)^2} \\ & = {x^2} + {y^2} + 2xy \\ & = 289 + 240 \\ & = 529 \\ & \therefore x + y \\ & = \sqrt {529} \\ & = 23 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the digit in the unit's place of a two-digit number is halved and the digit in the ten's place is doubled, the number thus obtained is equal to the number obtained by interchanging the digits. Which of the following is definitely true ?
o: Sum of the digits is a two-digit number
Digit in the unit's place is half of the digit in the ten's place
Digit in the unit's place and the ten's place are equal
Digit in the unit's place is twice the digit in the ten's place
s: Let the ten's digit be x and the unit's digit be y Then, number = 10x + y New number : $$\begin{aligned} & = 10 \times 2x + \frac{y}{2} \\ & = 20x + \frac{y}{2} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 20x + \frac{y}{2} = 10y + x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 40x + y = 20y + 2x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 38x = 19y \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 2x \end{aligned}$$ So, the unit's digit is twice the ten's digit.

q: The sum of the numerator and denominator of a fraction is 11. If 1 is added to the numerator and 2 is subtracted from the denominator, it becomes $$\frac{2}{3}$$. The fraction is :
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x + y = 11.....(\text{i}) \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 1}}{{y - 2}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3\left( {x + 1} \right) = 2\left( {y - 2} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3x - 2y = - 7.....(\text{ii}) \end{aligned}$$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get: x = 3 and y = 8 So, the fraction is $$\frac{3}{8}$$

q: In a Mathematics examination the number scored by 5 candidates are 5 successive odd integers. If their total marks are 185, the highest score is :
s: Let the five successive odd number be, x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6, x + 8 Then, according to given information, 185 = x + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6 + x + 8 $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 185 = 5x + 20 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5x = 185 - 20 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5x = 165 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 33 \end{aligned}$$ Highest number = 33 + 8 = 41

q: Three numbers are in in the ratio of 3 : 4 : 6 and their product is 1944. The largest of these numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be 3x, 4x and 6x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 3x \times 4x \times 6x = 1944 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 72{x^3} = 1944 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^3} = 27 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Largest number = 6x = 18

q: The sum of the squares of two numbers is 3341 and the difference of their squares is 891. The numbers are :
s: Let the numbers be x and y. Then, x 2 + y 2 = 3341..... (i) And, x 2 - y 2 = 891..... (ii) Adding (i) and (ii), we get : 2x 2 = 4232 or x 2 = 2116 or x = 46 Subtracting (ii) from (i), we get : 2y 2 = 2450 or y 2 = 1225 or y = 35 So, the numbers are 35 and 46

q: In a two-digit number, if it is known that its unit's digits exceeds its ten's digit by 2 and that the product of the given number and the sum of its digits is equal to 144, then the number is :
s: Let the ten's digit be x Then, unit's digit = x + 2 ∴ Number : = 10x + (x + 2) = 11x + 2 Sum of digits : = x + (x + 2) = 2x + 2 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {11x + 2} \right)\left( {2x + 2} \right) = 144 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 22{x^2} + 26x - 140 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 11{x^2} + 13x - 70 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 2} \right)\left( {11x + 35} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, required number: = 11x + 2 = 11× 2 + 2 = 24

q: The difference between the numerator and the denominator of a fraction is 5. If 5 is added to its denominator, the fraction is decreased by $$1\frac{1}{4}$$. Find the value of the fraction.
s: Let the denominator be x Then, numerator = x + 5 Now, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 5}}{x} - \frac{{x + 5}}{{x + 5}} = \frac{5}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 5}}{x} = \frac{5}{4} + 1 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 5}}{x} = \frac{9}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 5}}{x} = 2\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}$$ So, the fraction is $$2\frac{1}{4}$$

q: A number whose fifth part increased by 4 is equal to its fourth part diminished by 10, is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {\frac{1}{5}x + 4} \right) = \left( {\frac{1}{4}x - 10} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{{20}} = 14 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 14 \times 20 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 280 \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio between a two-digit number and the sum of the digits of that number is 4 : 1. If the digit in the unit's place is 3 more than the digit in the ten's place, then the number is ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x Then, units digit = x + 3 Number = 10x + (x + 3) = 11x + 3 Sum of digits = x + (x + 3) = 2x + 3 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{11x + 3}}{{2x + 3}} = \frac{4}{1} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 11x + 3 = 8x + 12 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3x = 9 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, Required number = 11x + 3 = 11 × 3 + 3 = 36

q: The difference between two positive integers is 3. If the sum of their squares is 369, then the sum of the numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be x and (x + 3) Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + {\left( {x + 3} \right)^2} = 369 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + {x^2} + 9 + 6x = 369 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2{x^2} + 6x - 360 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + 3x - 180 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 15} \right)\left( {x - 12} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 12 \end{aligned}$$ So, the numbers are 12 and 15 ∴ Required sum = (12 + 15) = 27

q: A number consists of two digits. If the digits interchange place and the new number is added to the original number, then the resulting number will be divisible by :
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, number = 10x + y Number obtained by interchanging the digits = 10y + x ∴ (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 11(x + y), which is divisible by 11

q: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 2 and the denominator is increased by 3, the fraction becomes $$\frac{7}{9}$$ and if both the numerator as well as he denominator are decreased by 1, the fraction becomes $$\frac{4}{5}$$. What is the original fraction ?
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 2}}{{y + 3}} = \frac{7}{9} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9x - 7y = 3.....(i) \\ & {\text{And,}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x - 1}}{{y - 1}} = \frac{4}{5} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5x - 4y = 1.....(ii) \end{aligned}$$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get : x = 5 and y = 6 Hence, the original fraction is $$\frac{5}{6}$$

q: The difference of two numbers is 20% of the larger number. If the smaller number is 12, the larger one is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x - 12 = 20\% {\text{ of }}x \\ & \Leftrightarrow x - \frac{x}{5} = 12 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{4x}}{5} = 12 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{12 \times 5}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 15 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two numbers are such that the ratio between them is 4 : 7. If each is increased by 4, the ratio becomes 3 : 5. The lager number is ?
s: Let the numbers be 4x and 7x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{4x + 4}}{{7x + 4}} = \frac{3}{5} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5\left( {4x + 4} \right) = 3\left( {7x + 4} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 8 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Larger number : = 7x = 7 × 8 = 56

q: the difference between two numbers is 3 and the difference between their squares is 63. Which is the larger number ?
s: Let the number be x and y Then, $${x^2} - {y^2} = 63\,\,\,\,\& \,\,\,\,x - y = 3$$ On dividing, we get: x + y = 21 Solving x + y = 21 and x - y = 3, We get: x = 12 and y = 9 ∴ Larger number = 12

q: twenty times a positive integer is less than its square by 96. What is the integer ?
s: Let the integer be x Them, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - 20x = 96 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - 20x - 96 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 4} \right)\left( {x - 24} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 24 \end{aligned}$$

q: There are two numbers such that the sum of twice the first number and thrice the second number is 100 and the sum of thrice the first number and twice the second number is 120. Which is the larger number ?
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, 2x + 3y = 100 ..... (i) And, 3x + 2y = 120 ..... (ii) Adding (i) and (ii), we get : 5x + 5y = 220 or x + y = 44 ..... (iii) Subtracting (i) from (ii): we get : x - y = 20 ..... (iv) Adding (iii) and (iv), we get : 2x = 64 or x = 32 Putting x = 32 in (iii), we get : y = 12 Hence, larger number = 32

q: If one-seventh of a number exceeds its eleventh part by 100, then the number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{7}x - \frac{1}{{11}}x = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{4x}}{{77}} = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{7700}}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 1925 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of three numbers is 264. If the first number be twice the second and third number be be one-third of the first, then the second number is :
s: Let the second number be x Then, first number = 2x, And third number = $$\frac{2x}{3}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 2x + x + \frac{{2x}}{3} = 264 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{11x}}{3} = 264 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{264 \times 3}}{{11}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 72 \end{aligned}$$

q: A, B, C, D and E are five consecutive odd numbers. The sum of A and C is 146. What is the value of E ?
s: Let A = x B = x + 2 C = x + 4 D = x + 6 and E = x + 8 Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow A + C = 146 \\ & \Rightarrow x + \left( {x + 4} \right) = 146 \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 142 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 71 \\ & \therefore E = x + 8 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 71 + 8 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 79 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the positions of its digits is 36. What is the difference between the two digits of the number ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {10x + y} \right) - \left( {10y + x} \right) = 36 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9\left( {x - y} \right) = 36 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x - y = 4 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by $$\frac{1}{4}$$ and the denominator is decreased byy $$\frac{1}{3}$$, the new fraction obtained is $$\frac{33}{64}$$. What was the original fraction ?
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + \frac{1}{4}}}{{y - \frac{1}{3}}} = \frac{{33}}{{64}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{3\left( {4x + 1} \right)}}{{4\left( {3y - 1} \right)}} = \frac{{33}}{{64}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{4x + 1}}{{3y - 1}} = \frac{{33}}{{64}} \times \frac{4}{3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{4x + 1}}{{3y - 1}} = \frac{{11}}{{16}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 16\left( {4x + 1} \right) = 11\left( {3y - 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 64x + 16 = 33y - 11 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 64x - 33y = - 27 \end{aligned}$$ Which cannot be solved to find $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Hence, the original fraction cannot be determined from the given data.

q: If doubling a number and adding 20 to the result gives the same answer as multiplying the number by 8 and taking away 4 from the product, the number is :
s: Let the number be x Then, ⇔ 2x + 20 = 8x - 4 ⇔ 6x = 24 ⇔ x = 4

q: Out of six consecutive natural numbers if the sum of first three is 27, what is the sum of the other three ?
The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the two digits is 63. Which is the smaller of the two numbers ?
s: Let the ten's digit be x and unit's digit be y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {10x + y} \right) - \left( {10y + x} \right) = 63 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9\left( {x - y} \right) = 63 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x - y = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 200% and the denominator is increased by 300%, the resultant fraction is $$\frac{15}{26}$$. What was the original fraction ?
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + 200\% {\text{ of }}x}}{{y + 300\% {\text{ of }}y}} = \frac{{15}}{{26}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{3x}}{{4y}} = \frac{{15}}{{26}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{{15}}{{26}} \times \frac{4}{3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{{10}}{{13}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If 50 is subtracted from two-third of number, the result is equal to sum of 40 and one-fourth of that number. What is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{2}{3}x - 50 = \frac{1}{4}x + 40 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{4}x = 90 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{5x}}{{12}} = 90 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{90 \times 12}}{5}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 216 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of two numbers is 25 and their difference is 13. Find their product :
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, x + y = 25 and x - y = 13 $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 4xy = {\left( {x + y} \right)^2} - {\left( {x - y} \right)^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4xy = {\left( {25} \right)^2} - {\left( {13} \right)^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4xy = 625 - 169 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4xy = 456 \\ & \Leftrightarrow xy = 114 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of seven consecutive numbers is 175. What is the difference between twice the largest number and thrice the smallest number ?
The number obtained by interchanging the two digits of a two-digit number is lesser than the original number by 54. If the sum of the two digit of the number is 12, then what is the original number ?
s: Let ten's digit = x Then, unit's digit = (12 - x) $$\therefore \left[ {10x + \left( {12 - x} \right)} \right] -$$ $$\left[ {10\left( {12 - x} \right) + x} \right]$$ $$= 54$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow 18x - 108 = 54 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 18x = 162 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 9 \end{aligned}$$ So, ten's digit = 9 and unit's digit = 3 Hence, original number = 93

q: A fraction is such that if the double of the numerator and the triple pf the denominator is changed by +10 percent and -30 percent respectively, then we get 11 percent of $$\frac{16}{21}$$. Find the fraction :
s: Let the fraction be $$\frac{x}{y}$$ Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{110\% {\text{ of 2}}x}}{{70\% {\text{ of 3}}y}} = 11\% {\text{ of }}\frac{{16}}{{21}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{22x}}{{21y}} = \frac{{11}}{{100}} \times \frac{{16}}{{21}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \left( {\frac{{11}}{{100}} \times \frac{{16}}{{21}} \times \frac{{21}}{{22}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{2}{{25}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A student was asked to divide the half of a certain number by 6 and the other half by 4 and then to add the two quantities so obtained. Instead of doing so the student divided the number by 5 and the result fell short by 4. The given number was ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left[ {\frac{{\left( {\frac{x}{2}} \right)}}{6} + \frac{{\left( {\frac{x}{2}} \right)}}{4}} \right] - \frac{x}{5} = 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{{12}} + \frac{x}{8} - \frac{x}{5} = 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{10x + 15x - 24x}}{{120}} = 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 4 \times 120 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 480 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the sum of numbers is 33 and their difference is 15, the smaller number is ?
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, $$x + y = 33.....(i)$$ And, $$x - y = 15.....(ii)$$ Solving (i) and (ii), we get : x = 24 , y = 9 ∴ Smaller number = 9

q: In a two-digit positive number, the digit in the unit's place is equal to the square of the digit in ten's place, and the difference between the number and the number obtained by interchanging the digits is 54. What is 40% of the original number ?
s: Let ten's digit = x Then, unit's digit = x 2 Then, number = 10x + x 2 Clearly, since x 2 > x, So, the number formed by interchanging the digits is greater than the original number. $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {10{x^2} + x} \right) - \left( {10x + {x^2}} \right) = 54 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9{x^2} - 9x = 54 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - x = 6 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - x - 6 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - 3x + 2x - 6 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 3} \right)\left( {x + 2} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3 \end{aligned}$$ So. ten's digit = 3, unit's digit = 3 2 = 9 ∴ Original number = 39 Required result : = 40% of 39 = 15.6

q: 243 has been divided into three parts such that half of the first part, one-third of the second part and one-fourth of the third part are equal. The largest part is :
s: Let the three parts be A, B and C $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let }}\frac{A}{2} = \frac{B}{3} = \frac{C}{4} = x \\ & {\text{Then, }}A = 2x,B = 3x{\text{ and }}C = 4x \\ & {\text{So, }}A:B:C = 2:3:4 \\ & \therefore {\text{Largest part :}} \\ & = \left( {243 \times \frac{4}{9}} \right) \\ & = 108 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the sum of a number and its square is 182, what is the number ?
s: Let the number be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x + {x^2} = 182 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} + x - 182 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + 14} \right)\left( {x - 13} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 13 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of two numbers is 40 and their difference is 4. The ratio of the numbers is :
s: Let the numbers be x and y Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + y}}{{x - y}} = \frac{{40}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{x + y}}{{x - y}} = 10 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x + y} \right) = 10\left( {x - y} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9x = 11y \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{{11}}{9} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x:y = 11:9 \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of three consecutive odd numbers and three consecutive even numbers together is 231. Also, the smallest odd number is 11 less than the smallest even number. What is the sum of the largest odd number and the largest even number ?
s: Let the three odd numbers be x, (x + 2), (x + 4) and The three even numbers be (x + 11), (x + 13) and (x + 15) Then, ⇔ x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) + (x + 11) + (x + 13) + (x + 15) = 231 ⇔ 6x + 45 = 231 ⇔ 6x = 186 ⇔ x = 31 ∴ Required sum : = (x + 4) + (x + 15) = 2x + 19 = 2 × 31 + 19 = 62 + 19 = 81

q: A number consists of 3 digits whose sum is 10. The middle digit is equal to the sum of the other two and the number will be increased by 99 if its digits are reversed. The number is :
s: Let the middle digit be x Then, 2x = 10 or x = 5 So, the number is either 253 or 352 Since the number increases on reversing the digits, so the hundred's digit is smaller than the unit's digit. Hence, required number = 253

q: The sum of four numbers is 64. If you add 3 to the first number, 3 is subtracted from the second number, the third is multiplied by 3 and the fourth is divided by 3, then all the results are equal. What is the difference between the largest and the smallest of the original numbers ?
s: Let the four numbers be , A, B, C and D Let A + 3 = B - 3 = 3C = $$\frac{D}{3}$$ = x Then, A = x - 3 B = x + 3 C = $$\frac{x}{3}$$ D = 3x $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow A + B + C + D = 64 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 3} \right) + \left( {x + 3} \right) + \frac{x}{3} + 3x = 64 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5x + \frac{x}{3} = 64 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 16x = 192 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 12 \end{aligned}$$ Thus, the numbers are 9, 15, 4 and 36 ∴ Required difference : = (36 - 4) = 32

q: The sum of five consecutive odd numbers is 575. What is the sum of the next set of five consecutive odd numbers ?
